title: Keep strict wall-clock speed checks out of the CI test run
description: On TASK-1.3's CI attempt 2 (run 44236421395), two pre-existing wall-clock tests failed on a slow shared GitHub runner although no related code changed: tests/engine/hand-evaluator.perf.test.ts reached 975,968 evals/s against its 1,000,000 floor, and tests/advice/equity.test.ts 'bounds the work…' took 2676 ms against a 2000 ms limit. Shared runners vary several-fold in speed, so hard wall-clock limits inside the CI suite make unrelated pushes go red. The real speed targets are already enforced by separate full-speed commands on the reference Mac (TASK-1.2 SPEC-12, TASK-7.1 SPEC-12). Follow-up from TASK-1.3 judge finding J-1-00.

nodes.title: Keep strict wall-clock speed checks out of the CI test run
Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given CI (environment variable CI=true), When npm test runs, Then no test fails solely because a wall-clock duration or throughput limit is exceeded; correctness assertions in those tests still run
Given a local run on the reference machine, When the documented full-speed commands run (hand evaluator and equity perf suites), Then the original speed targets are still enforced unchanged

Given the bounded-work test for infeasible equity ranges, When it runs in CI, Then it still proves the work is bounded (e.g. by counting operations or a generous CI-only time ceiling) rather than being removed
Given the README or perf test headers, When a developer reads them, Then they state which commands enforce the real speed targets and that CI does not
